seoTitle: Change Paragraph and Line Spacing on Squarespace
metaDescription: Learn how to adjust line height and letter spacing for body text on Squarespace using the built-in Style Editor, no CSS required.
intro: If your Squarespace text feels too cramped or too spread out, adjusting line height and letter spacing can make a big difference in readability. This guide covers using the built-in Style Editor, which works especially well on Squarespace 7.1 and newer templates.

steps.heading: Log into Squarespace
steps.body: Sign in and select the website you want to edit to open its dashboard.

steps.heading: Open the Style Editor
steps.body: Go to Design, then Site Styles or Fonts, depending on your template, to access typography controls.

steps.heading: Find Paragraph Styles
steps.body: Inside the Fonts panel, look for Paragraph Styles under Body Text to adjust spacing settings.

steps.heading: Adjust line height
steps.body: Increase or decrease line height to control the vertical space between lines of text.

steps.heading: Adjust letter spacing
steps.body: Fine-tune letter spacing to control how dense or airy your paragraphs appear.

steps.heading: Save your changes
steps.body: Click Save so your updated spacing goes live on your published site.

faq.question: Do I need to know CSS to change paragraph spacing on Squarespace?
faq.answer: No, the built-in Style Editor lets you adjust line height and letter spacing without writing any code.

faq.question: Where do I find paragraph spacing settings?
faq.answer: Go to Design, then Site Styles or Fonts, and look for Paragraph Styles under Body Text.

faq.question: What's the difference between line height and letter spacing?
faq.answer: Line height controls vertical space between lines, while letter spacing adjusts the horizontal space between characters.

faq.question: Does this work on Squarespace 7.1?
faq.answer: Yes, this method works especially well with Squarespace 7.1 and newer templates.

faq.question: Can I still use custom CSS for more control?
faq.answer: Yes, advanced users can explore custom CSS for finer control, though the built-in tools are enough for most needs.
